mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy shift that lowers discount rates for equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in 60% or more of periods where FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in 60% or more of triggered instances, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous weakening in labor market participation (rising UNRATE) and slowing job growth (PAYEMS growth < 0.1%) indicates a deteriorating economic outlook, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising UNRATE and PAYEMS growth < 0.1% fails to predict negative returns in 60% or more of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below its 12-month moving average during a supply shock regime signals reduced economic output, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in 60% or more of periods with INDPRO decline during supply shocks, or the Rank IC for INDPRO in supply shock regimes is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in housing starts below 1500.0 thousand units signals weak residential demand, reducing construction activity and consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls below 1500.0 (thousands of units) in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in 60% or more of triggered instances, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index above 2.5% annually signals persistent inflation that triggers monetary policy tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in 60% or more of periods with CPIAUCSL above 2.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index combined with a stable or rising federal funds rate indicates an inflationary environment without accommodative policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction of rising CPIAUCSL and stable FEDFUNDS fails to predict negative returns in 60% or more of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) below 1.0% during late-cycle expansion signals an economic deceleration that reduces corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in 60% or more of periods with GDPC1 growth below 1.0% in late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC for GDPC1 in late-cycle is below 0.03.
